brief: NDX has broken back above its 100-day moving average and reversed its short-term downtrend, even though only about 30% of NDX members trade above their own 50-day averages. The note treats that gap as fuel for a squeeze rather than a warning sign. A close above 30,400 in futures would tip the market into a full upside pain trade. Goldman's Sentiment Index has fallen to -0.9, its lowest in over a year, despite the index sitting only a few percent from all-time highs, and weak breadth looks disconnected from that price level, adding more potential fuel if participation broadens. Retail buying's early-month recovery is already fading, systematic and institutional investors have cut exposure, and AAII bulls have collapsed to a multi-week low, leaving cleaner positioning that the note argues supports a squeeze. Separately, UBS's hyperscalers index now trades at the S&P 500's forward multiple (still a premium to the equal-weighted index), SOX's P/E is near multi-year lows against oil, prompting a macro versus AI framing and interest in call structures, and asset-light AI plays like cybersecurity and data infrastructure are being rewarded even as NET and SNOW keep re-rating despite rising 10-year yields.
